title: Force, Mass and Acceleration in One Dimension
learningObjectives: Apply a = F_net/m with constant mass to determine one-dimensional acceleration from net force
Define acceleration as change in velocity divided by change in time and use it in the second law
Recognize that F = m*a requires constant mass and that force and acceleration are vector quantities acting per component direction

explanations.text: For an object with constant mass, acceleration is proportional to net force and inversely proportional to mass, expressed as F = m*a so that a = F_net/m in one dimension.

evidence.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

explanations.text: The form F = m*a is valid when mass stays constant during the time interval, and acceleration is defined as the change in velocity divided by the change in time.

evidence.quote: Remember that this relation is only good for objects that have a constant mass.
The change in velocity divided by the change in time is the definition of the acceleration a.

explanations.text: Force, acceleration, velocity and momentum have both magnitude and direction, so the one-dimensional equation applies to the chosen axis with sign indicating direction.

evidence.quote: The velocity, force, acceleration, and momentum have both a magnitude and a direction associated with them.
